import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Combine date and time into a single datetime object for easier analysis
df['datetime'] = pd.to_datetime(df['date'] + ' ' + df['time'])

# Extract hour of the day and day of the week
df['hour'] = df['datetime'].dt.hour
df['day_of_week'] = df['datetime'].dt.day_name()

# --- Data Aggregation ---
# Create a pivot table to summarize total sales by day of the week and hour
sales_by_hour_day = df.pivot_table(
    values='total',
    index='day_of_week',
    columns='hour',
    aggfunc='sum',
    fill_value=0
)

# Ensure the days of the week are in the correct order
day_order = ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday', 'Sunday']
sales_by_hour_day = sales_by_hour_day.reindex(day_order)

# --- Visualization ---
# Set the aesthetic style of the plots
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create the figure and axes
plt.figure(figsize=(18, 9))

# Create the heatmap
ax = sns.heatmap(
    sales_by_hour_day,
    cmap='viridis',  # Use a visually appealing and colorblind-friendly colormap
    linewidths=.5,
    annot=True,      # Annotate cells with sales values
    fmt='.0f',       # Format annotations as integers
    annot_kws={"size": 8}, # Adjust annotation font size
    cbar_kws={'label': 'Total Sales ($)'} # Add a label to the color bar
)

# --- Customization and Labeling ---
# Set the title and labels with appropriate font sizes
ax.set_title('Peak Sales Hours by Day of the Week', fontsize=20, pad=20, weight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Hour of the Day (24h format)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Day of the Week', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Improve readability of tick labels
plt.xticks(rotation=0, ha='center', fontsize=10)
plt.yticks(rotation=0, va='center', fontsize=10)

# Add a subtle grid to the plot for better separation
ax.grid(which='major', axis='both', linestyle='--', linewidth=0.5, color='lightgray')

# --- Save the Figure ---
# Save the final plot to a file
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
